To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the antimicrobial effectiveness of polycation copolyoxetanates increases with increasing alkyl chain length and that selectivity for bacterial kill over human cell lysis increases with increasing chain length.

the MIC of quaternary PEG copolyoxetanates for E. coli, S. aureaus and P. aerugnosa are dependent on the length of the alkyl chain and that the C8–50 copolyoxetatane is the most effective antimicrobial, with low cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity.

the antimicrobial effectiveness of PEG/alkyl chain quaternary ammoniumpolyoxetanes is highly correlated with the length of the alkyl chain, and the hemolytic and cytotoxic activities of the polymers are very low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and evaluation of a series of quaternary PEG copolyoxetanates with varying alkyl chain length.
a new class of antimicrobial copolyoxetanides that are effective against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria and have low hemolytic and cytotoxic activities.
the development of a new generation of antimicrobial polymers that are effective against a broad spectrum of bacteria and have low hemolytic and cytotoxic activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C8–50 polycation is the best of the Cx–50 polycations in terms of antimicrobial effectiveness with the lowest hemolytic and cytotoxic activities.
the Cx-50 polycation series shows good antimicrobial efficacy and low hemolytic and cytotoxic activity.
C8–50 is a highly effective antimicrobial with good biocompatibility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cx–50 copolyoxetenes with C6–50, C8–C10–50, C12–50, and C14–50 were effective antibacterials with good selectivity for bacterial kill.
the C8–50 copolyoxatane is the best antimicrobial in terms of MIC, efficacy, and biocompatibility, and it is a promising candidate for further study as a biocompatible antimicrobial coating.
PEG/ quaternary copolyoxetans have high antibacterial activity with low cytotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antimicrobial activity of quaternary PEG copolyoxetenes depends on the chain length of the quaternary ammonio moiety.
antimicrobial efficacy can be tuned with the alkyl chain length and the copolyoxetan backbone provides a platform for low cytotoxicity.
PEG/ quaternary copolyoxetenes have a broad range of MICs, and the most effective antimicrobi- als have alkyl chains between 6 and 12 carbons in length.
